passages.original: ἢ σὺ τολμήσεις εἰπεῖν, ὡς ἐλήρει μὲν Πλατῶν, ἐλήρει δὲ Ἰσοκράτης, ἐλήρει δὲ Σοφοκλῆς, οὐκ ἐσωφρόνει δὲ Γοργίας, οὐκ ᾔδει δ’ ἑαυτὸν ὁ Τυανεὺς ἐκεῖνος;
passages.english: Or will you dare to say that Plato was talking nonsense, that Isocrates was talking nonsense, that Sophocles was talking nonsense, that Gorgias was not in his right mind, and that the famous man of Tyana did not know himself?
passages.notes: "The man of Tyana" is presumably Apollonius of Tyana. "Did not know himself" (οὐκ ᾔδει ἑαυτόν) probably alludes to the Delphic maxim "know yourself".
